players.biography: Ellyse Perry is the greatest female cricketer of the modern era and possibly the finest all-round athlete in Australian sporting history. She has represented Australia in both cricket and football at international level. As a cricketer her batting and bowling are both of extraordinary quality — she is one of a tiny handful of women to average over 50 in Test cricket while also taking wickets consistently. She was named ICC Women's Cricketer of the Decade (2010-2020). She has won multiple World Cups and the Ashes with Australia. Her excellence, elegance, and sportsmanship make her a true champion.
achievements: ICC Women's Cricketer of the Decade
fun_facts: She has played international cricket AND football for Australia
She is one of very few women to average over 50 in Test cricket
She was named Australia's most admired female athlete in multiple polls
players.style: Elegant batting technique, sharp medium-pace bowling, brilliant fielding, complete all-rounder

players.name: Meg Lanning
players.biography: Meg Lanning is the most successful captain in women's cricket history. Under her leadership Australia dominated women's cricket for a decade, winning multiple World Cups and remaining ranked number one almost continuously. The right-handed batter is a prolific run-scorer, particularly dominant in T20 cricket, and is one of the fastest scorers in Women's T20 internationals. She captained Australia to the 2020 T20 World Cup final at the MCG in front of 86,174 fans — a world record attendance for a women's cricket match. She retired temporarily from cricket in 2022 to focus on mental health before returning to lead Australia.
achievements: Multiple ICC Women's T20 World Cup winner
Multiple ICC Women's ODI World Cup winner
Most successful women's cricket captain ever
Record attendance at her World Cup final (86,174)
fun_facts: Her World Cup final at the MCG was watched by over 86,000 fans — a world record for women's cricket
She has won more World Cups as captain than any other women's cricket captain
She took time away from cricket to focus on mental health — inspiring many athletes to do the same
players.style: Powerful strokeplay, excellent timing, aggressive T20 batting, composed under pressure, inspirational captain

players.name: Mithali Raj
players.biography: Mithali Raj is India's greatest female cricketer and the highest run-scorer in the history of women's international cricket. The elegant right-hander from Rajasthan made her debut at 16 and went on to score over 10,000 international runs across all formats — an extraordinary achievement. She captained India to the Women's ODI World Cup final in 2017 — the closest India has come to winning the tournament. Her grace, technique, and mental strength made her one of the most respected players in women's cricket globally. She retired in 2022 as a national icon who had transformed Indian women's cricket into a major sport.
achievements: All-time leading run-scorer in women's cricket
fun_facts: She scored more runs in women's international cricket than anyone else in history
She is one of only a few women to score over 10,000 international runs
She inspired an entire generation of Indian girls to play cricket
players.style: Classical batting technique, excellent cover drives, mental resilience, consistent run-scoring over 23 years

players.name: Belinda Clark
players.biography: Belinda Clark is one of the greatest batters in women's cricket history and Australia's first women's cricket legend. The New South Wales captain was a dominating player who led Australia to World Cup glory in 1997 and 2005. She was the first cricketer — male or female — to score a double century in One Day International cricket, making 229* against Denmark in the 1997 World Cup. She captained Australia with authority and tactical intelligence for 10 years. After retiring she became a major figure in cricket administration, helping grow the women's game across Australia.
achievements: First-ever ODI double century (229* vs Denmark)
fun_facts: She scored the first ever double century by any cricketer in ODI cricket
She captained Australia to two World Cup victories
She became a key figure in growing women's cricket in Australia after retiring
players.style: Powerful top-order batting, elegant strokeplay, assured captaincy, dominant against weaker attacks

players.name: Heather Knight
players.biography: Heather Knight has been England women's most important cricketer of her generation, leading the team as captain with great tactical intelligence and consistency. The Devon-born batter captained England to the Women's World Cup in 2017 — England's greatest moment in women's cricket — beating India in a dramatic final. She is one of England's most consistent run-scorers and was named ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year in 2017. Known for her quiet leadership style and ability to bat through difficult situations, she has been England's rock in both Test and limited-overs cricket for over a decade.
achievements: ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year 2017
fun_facts: She led England to their World Cup victory on home soil in 2017
She is known for her calm, tactical approach to captaincy
She studied marine biology before pursuing cricket professionally
players.style: Patient top-order batting, strong square drives, excellent under pressure, calm tactical captaincy

players.name: Smriti Mandhana
players.biography: Smriti Mandhana is India's most exciting and aesthetically pleasing batter — a left-hander whose shots through the covers and over the infield are among the most beautiful in the women's game. The Pune-born opener has won the ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year award twice and is consistently ranked as one of the world's top women's batters. Her ability to set up big totals at the top of the innings with aggressive, technically sound batting has made her India's most important batting asset. She is also a key figure in building cricket's popularity among young girls in India.
achievements: 2x ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year
Multiple half-centuries and centuries at ODI and T20 level
fun_facts: She won the ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year award twice
She is known for having the most beautiful cover drives in women's cricket
She once scored four consecutive centuries in international cricket
players.style: Elegant left-handed strokeplay, stunning cover drives, aggressive opening, technically perfect technique

players.name: Charlotte Edwards
players.biography: Charlotte Edwards was England women's cricket captain for 11 years and the most important figure in the growth of women's cricket in England. The Kent batter was a prolific run-scorer who helped England win the Women's World Cup in 2009 and the ICC Women's Championship. Scoring over 5,000 ODI runs, she was one of England's most reliable and consistent performers for two decades. Her leadership helped professionalise the England women's game and paved the way for the Hundred and the new era of women's cricket in England. She was awarded a CBE for services to cricket.
fun_facts: She captained England for 11 years — a record
She helped transform women's cricket into a professional sport in England
She scored her first century for England at just 16 years old
players.style: Compact top-order batting, strong square cuts, consistent big-match performer, experienced leader

players.name: Ricky Ponting
players.biography: Ricky Ponting is Australia's greatest captain and arguably the best batsman in the world of his era. The Tasmanian led Australia to back-to-back World Cup victories (2003, 2007) and during his captaincy Australia achieved a world-record 16 consecutive Test wins. He scored 13,378 Test runs — second all-time behind Sachin Tendulkar — and was a dominant figure with the pull shot and cover drive. His 140* in the 2003 World Cup final against India remains one of the finest innings in the tournament's history. Ponting was intense, aggressive, and relentless — the embodiment of Australian cricket's winning culture.
achievements: Wisden Cricketer of the Year twice
fun_facts: He led Australia to 16 consecutive Test wins — a world record
His 140* in the 2003 World Cup final vs India was one of the greatest ever ODI innings
He is only the second player to score 13,000+ Test runs
players.style: Dominant pull shot, textbook cover drives, aggressive captaincy, relentless competitive hunger

players.name: Adam Gilchrist
players.biography: Adam Gilchrist revolutionised cricket's wicketkeeper-batsman role. He was simultaneously the world's best keeper and one of the most destructive opening batsmen ever produced — an almost impossible combination. His attacking style and ability to change a game in 10 overs changed how teams approached their batting line-ups. He scored 9,619 Test runs at a strike rate far exceeding any other keeper-bat of his era. His 57-ball century in the 2007 World Cup final against Sri Lanka — where he hid a squash ball inside his glove for grip — remains one of cricket's most extraordinary batting performances. He helped Australia win three World Cups.
achievements: Fastest ever wicketkeeper to 100 Test dismissals
ICC Wicketkeeper of the Year multiple times
2007 World Cup final century in 57 balls
fun_facts: He famously walked when he knew he was out — even in an Ashes Test — when the umpire didn't give him out
He hid a squash ball inside his glove in the 2007 World Cup final
He once scored a century in 57 balls in a World Cup final
players.style: Explosive left-handed batting, safe hands behind the stumps, attacking cricket from ball one

players.name: Glenn McGrath
players.biography: Glenn McGrath is the greatest fast bowler of his era and one of the most accurate in cricket history. The New South Wales farmer turned relentless precision into an art form, consistently landing the ball on the same spot outside off-stump until batsmen made mistakes. He took 563 Test wickets — a world record for a pace bowler at the time of his retirement — and 381 ODI wickets. He was a devastating predator against top batsmen, particularly left-handers and England's top order. His pre-tournament predictions were legendary: before the 2003 World Cup he predicted Australia would win 5-0 — they won 4-0 against England.
achievements: 563 Test wickets (former world record for pace)
fun_facts: He predicted before major matches who he would dismiss — and was often right
He took 5 wickets in an innings against England 8 times in Ashes cricket
His foundation, McGrath Foundation, raises awareness for breast cancer
players.style: Metronomic line and length, movement away from the bat, relentless patience, devastating accuracy

players.name: Viv Richards
players.biography: Viv Richards was the most feared batsman of his generation and perhaps the most dominant personality cricket has ever seen. The Antiguan walked to the wicket without a helmet, chewing gum, and exuded an aura of total confidence that intimidated even the fastest bowlers. He scored at a strike rate unmatched for a Test player of his era and took apart the world's best bowling attacks with an aggression that bordered on contemptuous. He led West Indies to World Cup glory in 1975 and 1979 and captained the most successful Test team of all time. His fastest-ever Test century — in 56 balls — remains the benchmark of aggressive batting.
fun_facts: He batted without a helmet throughout his career — against the world's fastest bowlers
His fastest Test century took just 56 balls — a record for many years
He never lost a Test series as West Indies captain
players.style: Dominant aggressive batting, powerful pulls and cuts, mental intimidation, refused to wear a helmet

players.name: Curtly Ambrose
players.biography: Curtly Ambrose was the most feared fast bowler of the 1990s — a 6ft 7in Antiguan giant who could make the ball lift to chest height from a good length. His late movement and ability to trouble even the best batsmen with steep bounce made him almost unplayable on helpful pitches. He took 405 Test wickets at an average of 20.99 — one of the best bowling averages for any pace bowler with 400+ wickets. His spell of 7-1 in 33 balls against Australia in 1993 — including dismissing three batsmen for ducks — is considered one of the greatest bowling performances in cricket history.
fun_facts: His 7-1 spell against Australia in 1993 is one of the greatest ever bowling performances
He almost never spoke to batsmen — his cricket did all the talking
He is a talented bass guitarist and plays in a band
players.style: Steep bounce from great height, late movement, quiet menace, lethal short ball, devastating accuracy

players.name: Kapil Dev
players.biography: Kapil Dev is India's greatest all-rounder and the man who won India their first-ever Cricket World Cup in 1983. The Haryana Hurricane was a genuine all-rounder who bowled fast, outswinging deliveries and batted with explosive power down the order. He led India to their miracle 1983 World Cup victory — 66-1 against the mighty West Indies — in one of cricket's greatest upsets. His 175* against Zimbabwe in the same tournament, scored when India were 17/5, is still considered the greatest innings under pressure in World Cup history. He took 434 Test wickets — a world record at the time of his retirement.
achievements: 175* vs Zimbabwe (1983 World Cup — greatest recovery innings)
Wisden Indian Cricketer of the Century
fun_facts: He scored 175* when India were 17 for 5 — no cameras were available that day and the innings was never recorded
He led India to a miracle World Cup victory that nobody expected
He was the first player to take 400 Test wickets AND score 5,000 Test runs
players.style: Swerving outswing, explosive batting, fierce competitive spirit, never-say-die leadership

players.name: Sunil Gavaskar
players.biography: Sunil Gavaskar is India's first batting superstar and the man who defined what it meant to open the batting against the world's fastest bowlers without a helmet. The 'Little Master' from Mumbai scored 10,122 Test runs — the first batsman in history to pass 10,000 Test runs — and was the world's leading Test run scorer on retirement. He batted against Michael Holding, Malcolm Marshall, and Andy Roberts — the fastest bowlers in the world — with immense skill and courage. He scored 34 Test centuries — another world record at the time. He inspired an entire generation of Indian cricketers including the young Sachin Tendulkar.
fun_facts: He was the first batsman in history to score 10,000 Test runs
He inspired the young Sachin Tendulkar to become a cricketer
He once batted the entire 60-over ODI for 174* in the 1975 World Cup — but India were bowled out for 60 runs chasing 335
players.style: Technically perfect, impenetrable defence, swift footwork against pace, composed temperament

players.name: Rahul Dravid
players.biography: Rahul Dravid, 'The Wall', is India's most dependable and technically perfect Test batsman. His iron-hard defence, the most correct technique in the game, and extraordinary concentration allowed him to bat for hours and sessions when others faltered. He scored 13,288 Test runs at an average of 52.31 and holds the record for the most catches by a non-wicketkeeper in Test cricket. He saved many of India's greatest Tests through sheer determination and skill. Perhaps even more impressive than his playing career is his subsequent success as India's national team coach, guiding India to the T20 World Cup in 2024.
achievements: Most catches by non-keeper in Tests
India head coach (T20 World Cup 2024 winner)
fun_facts: He is nicknamed 'The Wall' because he was almost impossible to get out
He holds the record for the most catches by any non-wicketkeeper in Tests
As India's coach he led them to the T20 World Cup title in 2024
players.style: Technically perfect defence, extraordinary concentration, composure in any situation, reliable under pressure

players.name: MS Dhoni
players.biography: MS Dhoni is the greatest captain in Indian cricket history and one of the most successful white-ball captains in world cricket. The boy from Ranchi who styled his hair like a famous rock star became a national hero when he hit a six to win the 2011 World Cup final — the winning moment was celebrated by over a billion people. Dhoni's calm under pressure, helicopter shot, and lightning-fast stumpings made him one of the game's most complete and unique players. He won the T20 World Cup in 2007, the 50-over World Cup in 2011, and the Champions Trophy in 2013 — the only captain to have won all three major ICC trophies.
achievements: ODI World Cup 2011 (six to win — winning blow)
4x IPL title with Chennai Super Kings
Only captain to win all ICC major trophies
fun_facts: He hit the six that won India the 2011 World Cup in front of 1 billion watching Indians
His helicopter shot is one of the most copied batting techniques in cricket
He was a soldier in the Indian Territorial Army
players.style: Cool captaincy, helicopter shot, fastest stumpings in history, composed under pressure, intuitive cricket brain

players.name: Imran Khan
players.biography: Imran Khan is Pakistan's greatest cricketer and one of the finest all-rounders in cricket history. The Oxford-educated fast-bowling all-rounder inspired Pakistan to their only Cricket World Cup victory in 1992 — his famous 'cornered tigers' speech galvanising a team on the brink of elimination. As a bowler he was genuinely fast and had reverse swing as a lethal weapon. As a batsman he could play elegant shots or slog when needed. He rebuilt the Pakistan bowling attack almost single-handedly throughout the 1970s and 80s. After retiring from cricket he entered Pakistani politics and became Prime Minister.
achievements: First Pakistan player to perform the double of 300 wickets and 3,000 runs
fun_facts: His 'cornered tigers' speech before Pakistan's do-or-die World Cup matches in 1992 is legendary
He went on to become Prime Minister of Pakistan after retiring from cricket
He built a cancer hospital in Pakistan dedicated to his mother who died from cancer
players.style: Genuinely fast bowling, reverse swing pioneer, powerful lower-order batting, inspirational leadership

players.name: Pat Cummins
players.biography: Pat Cummins is the best fast bowler in the world and one of the finest cricket captains Australia has ever produced. The Sydney-born pace bowler consistently ranks at or near the top of the ICC bowling rankings and has an ability to take wickets even when conditions don't favour him. He led Australia to the World Test Championship title in 2023 and to an Ashes series win. His 2023 ODI World Cup campaign saw him captain Australia to the tournament victory. Cummins combines exceptional bowling with genuine batting ability and is also notable for his advocacy on climate change — a rare cricketer willing to speak publicly on environmental issues.
achievements: World No.1 Test bowler multiple times
fun_facts: He is the only player to captain Australia to World Test Championship AND ODI World Cup in the same year
He speaks publicly about climate change — unusual for a professional sportsman
He took a wicket on his Test debut — then was injured and couldn't play for six years
players.style: Explosive pace, late swing, reverse swing, exceptional at death bowling, intelligent attacking captain

players.name: Rohit Sharma
players.biography: Rohit Sharma is India's most elegant batsman of his generation and the only player in history to score three ODI double centuries. The Mumbai opener is nicknamed 'The Hitman' for his ability to take apart any bowling attack with powerful, effortless strokeplay. His flat-bat pull, six-hitting ability, and smooth timing make him one of cricket's most aesthetically pleasing batsmen. He captained India to the T20 World Cup victory in 2024 — finally ending India's ICC trophy drought. His 264 against Sri Lanka in 2014 remains the highest ODI individual score in history. As Mumbai Indians captain he won the IPL five times.
fun_facts: He is the only player ever to score three double centuries in ODI cricket
His 264 vs Sri Lanka is the highest ever individual score in ODI cricket
He won the T20 World Cup as captain at age 37
players.style: Effortless timing, powerful six-hitting, flat-bat pull shot, composed under pressure, natural elegance

players.name: Brett Lee
players.biography: Brett Lee was the fastest bowler of his era — a blond-haired, blue-eyed pace machine who regularly clocked 155 km/h and was one of cricket's most thrilling spectacles. Lee worked with cricket's great bowling coaches to add swing, variation, and yorkers to his raw pace. He took 310 Test wickets and 380 ODI wickets for Australia and helped his side win multiple Ashes series and World Cups. His ability to bowl at top pace in the death overs made him invaluable in the shorter formats. He was also a talented musician, a passionate supporter of charities in India, and one of cricket's most beloved personalities.
fun_facts: He regularly bowled over 155 km/h — consistently one of the fastest in the world
He is a talented musician who has released pop songs in Australia and India
He has done enormous charity work in India
players.style: Pure raw pace, lethal yorker, reverse swing, express delivery, exuberant and crowd-pleasing

players.name: Javed Miandad
players.biography: Javed Miandad is Pakistan's greatest-ever batsman and one of the shrewdest cricketing minds the sport has ever seen. The Karachi-born batsman had the ability to rescue any situation through guile, improvisation, and sheer fighting spirit. His last-ball six against India in the 1986 Austral-Asia Cup final — off Chetan Sharma's full toss with Pakistan needing 4 off the last ball — is the most celebrated shot in Pakistani cricket history. He played in six World Cups (a record) and averaged 52.57 in Tests, scoring 8,832 runs — the highest by any Pakistani player. He won the 1992 World Cup as part of Imran Khan's side.
achievements: Most capped Pakistan batsman of his era
fun_facts: His last-ball six in the 1986 final against India is the most celebrated shot in Pakistan cricket history
He appeared in six different World Cup tournaments
He was equally brilliant at Test and ODI cricket despite completely different demands
players.style: Street-smart batting, improvised shots, fighting against the odds, brilliant running between wickets

players.name: Anil Kumble
players.biography: Anil Kumble is India's greatest wicket-taker and one of the finest spin bowlers in the history of cricket. The Bangalore-born leg-spinner took 619 Test wickets — the third highest tally in history — with a skidding, accurate style unlike any other leg-spinner. Unlike traditional leg-spinners who flight the ball, Kumble bowled at pace and got sharp bounce. He is only the second bowler in history to take all 10 wickets in a Test innings — his 10 for 74 against Pakistan in Delhi in 1999 is one of cricket's greatest individual bowling performances. He took his final wicket with a fractured jaw, bowling through bandages to take a wicket against West Indies.
achievements: Only 2nd bowler to take all 10 wickets in an innings (10/74 vs Pakistan)
fun_facts: He took all 10 wickets in a Test innings — only the 2nd bowler in history to do so
He once bowled with a fractured jaw — bandaged up — and took a crucial wicket
He became a successful tech entrepreneur after retiring from cricket
players.style: Skiddy medium-pace leg spin, sharp turn from rough, never-ending accuracy, fierce competitor

players.name: Matthew Hayden
players.biography: Matthew Hayden was the most aggressive and powerful opening batsman of his era — a Queensland bull of a man who intimidated bowlers with his size, footwork, and enormous power. He partnered Justin Langer in one of cricket's finest opening partnerships and together they set the platform for Australia's dominant era. Hayden held the world record for the highest Test score — 380 against Zimbabwe in 2003 — for two years. His footwork down the wicket against spin made him exceptional in Asia, and his pull shot was one of cricket's most feared strokes. His cooking shows and charitable work in India gave him a popularity beyond cricket.
achievements: Held world Test record (380) for 2 years
fun_facts: He temporarily held the world record for the highest individual Test score with 380
He became famous in India for his cooking — particularly making curry
His footwork against spin was so good that many considered him Australia's best ever player of spin
players.style: Powerful front-foot play, ferocious pull shot, aggressive use of feet to spinners, intimidating presence

players.name: Michael Holding
players.biography: Michael Holding, 'Whispering Death', is the most graceful fast bowler in cricket history and many experts' choice as the fastest. His smooth, silent run-up — so quiet batsmen couldn't hear him coming — combined with explosive delivery pace terrified batsmen worldwide. His 14 wickets at The Oval in 1976 — the finest fast bowling performance in Ashes history — announced him to the world. A 1976 over to Brian Close where he hit the England captain multiple times with short balls is still shown as an example of fast bowling's power. After retiring he became one of cricket's finest commentators and a powerful voice against racism.
achievements: Best match figures: 14/149 at The Oval 1976
West Indies speed attack alongside Roberts, Marshall, Garner
fun_facts: Batsmen couldn't hear him approaching because his run-up was completely silent
His nickname 'Whispering Death' came from how silently he ran to bowl
He delivered one of cricket's most powerful speeches against racism in 2020
players.style: Silent run-up, explosive pace from smooth approach, sharp away movement, lethal bouncer

players.name: Clive Lloyd
players.biography: Clive Lloyd was the captain who built West Indies into the most dominant team in cricket history. The gentle giant from Georgetown created the greatest team the game has ever seen by assembling four of the fastest bowlers in the world — Roberts, Holding, Marshall, and Garner — and backed them to destroy every opponent. He led West Indies to two World Cup victories (1975, 1979) and presided over a run of 27 Test series without a defeat that stretched over 15 years. As a batsman he was a powerful, left-handed six-hitter. His legacy is the golden era of Caribbean cricket and a West Indies team that ruled the world.
fun_facts: He built West Indies into the most dominant team in cricket history
West Indies under his leadership went 27 Test series without losing
He assembled one of sport's most feared bowling attacks
players.style: Powerful left-handed batting, six-hitting ability, brilliant catching in the outfield, great tactical captain

players.name: Steve Waugh
players.biography: Steve Waugh was Australia's most resilient and mentally strong captain — a man who built a team culture of 'mental disintegration' that opponents found overwhelming. The twin from Canterbury scored 10,927 Test runs and earned the nickname 'Tugga' for his tenacity and unwillingness to give his wicket away. His famous hundred against England at the SCG in 2002-03 Ashes — off the last ball before the tea interval, having been dropped several times — was among cricket's most dramatic individual performances. He led Australia to 15 consecutive Ashes series wins and built a team many regard as the greatest in history.
fun_facts: He scored a famous century against England off the last ball before tea interval in an Ashes Test
He called his team's psychological tactics 'mental disintegration'
He is a passionate humanitarian who works extensively with lepers in India through Udayan Care
players.style: Unshakeable defence, mental toughness, brilliant captain, never-say-die batting, relentless competitor

players.name: David Warner
players.biography: David Warner was Australia's most devastating opening batsman of the modern era — a left-hander who attacked from the first ball and scored at a rate that set the tone for his team's innings. His technique, though unorthodox, was remarkably effective, combining a powerful slog-sweep, a lethal pull, and brilliant hands for cuts and drives. He holds the joint-record for the highest individual Test score for Australia (335*) and was the first Australian to score 1,000 Test runs in three separate calendar years. He won three World Cups for Australia and was the dominant figure in Australia's T20 World Cup victory in 2021.
achievements: IPL Orange Cap winner multiple times
fun_facts: He was the first Australian to score 1,000 Test runs in three different calendar years
He is one of the most dangerous limited-overs batsmen of his generation
His partnership with Matt Renshaw in Tests once featured a 200 run opening stand in 30 overs
players.style: Explosive left-handed attack, lethal pull and cut, brutal slog-sweep, sets aggressive early tone

players.name: Malcolm Marshall
players.biography: Malcolm Marshall is widely considered the greatest fast bowler in cricket history. The Barbadian speed merchant combined genuine pace with late swing, reverse swing, and cutters to create an almost unstoppable combination. He took 376 Test wickets at an average of 20.94 — the best average for any bowler with 200+ wickets. In 1984 he bowled with a fractured thumb in a plaster cast, unable to grip the bat, yet still took 7 wickets in the match. His ability to make the ball swing at high speed — something most fast bowlers cannot do — made him uniquely devastating. He died tragically of colon cancer at just 41.
achievements: 376 Test wickets at 20.94 (best average for 200+ wickets)
Took 7 wickets with a fractured thumb in plaster
fun_facts: He bowled with his thumb in plaster and took 7 wickets in a Test match
His 20.94 average is the best by any bowler with over 200 Test wickets
He is consistently rated the best fast bowler in Test cricket history
players.style: Lethal pace plus late swing, reverse swing, cutters, deadly yorker, complete fast bowling package

players.name: Allan Border
players.biography: Allan Border was the man who rebuilt Australian cricket from its lowest point. When he became Australia's captain in 1984 they were considered one of the worst Test teams in the world. Through sheer personal example, fight, and determination he gradually built them into world-beaters. He scored 11,174 Test runs — the world record on his retirement — playing more Test cricket than any Australian before him. His gritty, difficult-to-remove batting style and left-arm spin made him a valuable all-round player. The Allan Border Medal — Australia's player of the year award — is named in his honour.
achievements: Most Test appearances for Australia at the time
Allan Border Medal named in his honour
fun_facts: He once refused to speak to England players during an Ashes series to maintain competitive focus
He rebuilt Australian cricket from being one of the worst teams to world champions
His refusal to give up when Australia were at their lowest inspired an entire generation
players.style: Gritty determination, difficult to dismiss, left-arm spin, fighting spirit, total commitment to team

players.name: Mark Taylor
players.biography: Mark Taylor was one of Australia's finest captains and a reliable, technically sound opening batsman who provided solidity at the top of the order during Australia's rise to world dominance. The New South Welshman scored 7,525 Test runs and held an Australian record 157* at Headingley in 1989 before Dean Jones bettered it. His moment of grace came in Pakistan in 1998 when he declared his innings — he was on 334* and could have broken Don Bradman's record of 334 — choosing to share the honour rather than take it alone. He is widely considered one of the finest and most gracious men to have captained Australia.
achievements: Ashes series winner twice as captain
Declared at 334* to honour Bradman's record
fun_facts: He declared his innings at 334* — the same as Bradman's Australian record — out of respect
He is considered one of the most gracious sportsmen ever to captain Australia
He won consecutive Ashes series as captain
players.style: Technically correct opening batting, sure hands in the slip cordon, outstanding tactical captaincy

players.name: Roger Federer
players.biography: Roger Federer is widely considered the most graceful player in tennis history and spent a record 310 weeks as world number one. His game was defined by an almost unnatural elegance — flowing movement, silky serve, a one-handed backhand of rare beauty, and an ability to produce winners from anywhere on court. He won 20 Grand Slam titles including a record (at the time) 8 Wimbledon championships. His rivalry with Nadal — particularly the 2008 Wimbledon final, rated by many as the greatest tennis match ever played — defined an era. He finally retired in 2022, bowing out in tears at the Laver Cup alongside Nadal.

He played his last professional match alongside Rafael Nadal (his greatest rival) at the Laver Cup 2022
He once held all four Grand Slams simultaneously (2004–05)
players.style: Effortless grace, all-court player, exceptional serve, stunning one-handed backhand, brilliant net play

players.name: Rafael Nadal
players.biography: Rafael Nadal is the greatest clay-court player in history and holds the record with Novak Djokovic for most Grand Slam titles at 22. His 14 French Open titles at Roland Garros is a record in any single Grand Slam. 'Rafa' transformed tennis through extraordinary physical intensity — his top-spin forehand is the most powerful the game has ever seen. Born in Mallorca, Spain, he is known equally for his mental toughness: he won the French Open despite severe knee injuries that would have ended other careers. He retired from professional tennis in November 2024 after an emotional Davis Cup finals tie for Spain.
achievements: 22 Grand Slam titles (joint record with Djokovic)
14× French Open Champion — all-time record at any Grand Slam
Davis Cup Winner with Spain 5 times

players.style: Brutal topspin forehand, indestructible defence, ferocious intensity, supreme athlete, mental giant

players.name: Novak Djokovic
players.biography: Novak Djokovic holds the all-time record for Grand Slam titles with 24 and has been world number one for more weeks than any other player in history (428+). Born in Serbia, he grew up practising tennis in bombed-out Belgrade during the NATO strikes of 1999, sleeping in a bombed swimming pool. His rise to the top was built on extraordinary defensive ability — his flexibility is almost superhuman — combined with a two-handed backhand that is the best shot in tennis history. He is the only player to have won all four Grand Slams at least three times each (the 'Nole Slam') and won the 2023 French Open to achieve a Calendar Grand Slam in the Open Era.

3+ titles each at all four Grand Slams

players.name: Serena Williams
players.biography: Serena Williams is the greatest women's tennis player of all time and one of the greatest athletes in any sport. She won 23 Grand Slam singles titles — a record in the Open Era — and spent a total of 319 weeks as world number one. Born in Compton, California, she and her sister Venus were trained by their father Richard on crumbling public courts. She won the Australian Open in 2017 while eight weeks pregnant and returned to professional tennis after childbirth complications that nearly took her life. Her serve and forehand were the most dominant weapons women's tennis has ever seen, and she could overpower opponents in ways no player had before.

7× Australian Open, 7× Wimbledon, 6× US Open, 3× French Open

players.name: Steffi Graf
players.biography: Steffi Graf is the most dominant tennis player of any gender in the Open Era. The German's 'Golden Slam' in 1988 — winning all four Grand Slams AND the Olympic gold in a single calendar year — has never been matched by anyone. She held the world number one ranking for an incredible 377 weeks — the longest in tennis history. Her forehand is widely regarded as the greatest groundstroke in tennis history, and her speed around the court was extraordinary. She won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and retired at 30 — still the world's best player. She later married Andre Agassi.
achievements: Golden Slam 1988 (all four Slams + Olympic gold)

Her 377 weeks at world No.1 is the longest ever in tennis history
Her forehand is described by experts as the greatest tennis shot ever hit

players.name: Martina Navratilova
players.biography: Martina Navratilova is the greatest tennis player in terms of total titles won, having accumulated 167 singles titles over a career spanning more than 30 years. She won 18 Grand Slam singles titles and is probably the most complete tennis player ever: she had serve-and-volley skills, incredible athleticism, and pioneered modern sports science in tennis. She defected from communist Czechoslovakia in 1975 and became an American citizen. She fought for gay rights throughout her career and later in life. She won singles titles at Wimbledon a record nine times. Her rivalry with Chris Evert is one of sport's greatest.
fun_facts: She won 167 career titles — more than any tennis player in history
She defected from Czechoslovakia to pursue her tennis career
She won Wimbledon nine times — the most any player has ever won it
players.style: Serve-and-volley genius, exceptional net game, athletic excellence, all-surface dominance

players.name: Chris Evert
players.biography: Chris Evert was the most consistent baseline player in tennis history and won 18 Grand Slam titles. Her two-handed backhand — which she introduced and popularised — revolutionised the game and is now standard technique for millions of players worldwide. Known as 'The Ice Maiden' for her cool composure under pressure, she never once lost in the first round at a Grand Slam across a career spanning 19 years. Her Roland Garros record — winning the French Open seven times and losing only once there in her entire career — is one of sport's greatest statistical achievements. Her rivalry with Martina Navratilova is one of tennis's finest.

At Roland Garros she lost just once — her record there was 72-1

players.style: Pinpoint baseline accuracy, ice-cool composure, pioneering two-handed backhand, relentless consistency

players.name: Billie Jean King
players.biography: Billie Jean King is the most important person in the history of women's sport. She won 12 Grand Slam singles titles and was world number one six times, but her legacy extends far beyond tennis. In 1973 she played Bobby Riggs — a 55-year-old self-proclaimed 'male chauvinist' — in the famous 'Battle of the Sexes' in front of 90 million TV viewers and beat him 6-4, 6-3, 6-3. She fought for equal prize money in tennis and won — the US Open became the first Grand Slam to offer equal pay in 1973. She is a champion of LGBTQ+ rights. The tennis courts at the US Open venue are named after her.

Fought for equal pay in tennis

players.name: Venus Williams
players.biography: Venus Williams is a tennis trailblazer who, alongside her younger sister Serena, transformed the power game in women's tennis. The older Williams sister won seven Grand Slam singles titles and is a five-time Wimbledon champion. Her powerful serving — among the fastest in women's tennis history — and aggressive baseline game made her a dominant force in the 2000s. She fought for equal prize money at Wimbledon and succeeded — in 2007 Wimbledon began offering equal pay. She has also built a successful interior design business and fashion line. Her bond with Serena — often playing each other in finals — is one of sport's most remarkable sibling stories.

players.name: Margaret Court
players.biography: Margaret Court holds the record for the most Grand Slam singles titles in tennis history — 24 — more than any man or woman ever. The Australian dominated women's tennis throughout the 1960s and early 1970s, winning the Australian Open 11 times when it was the most prestigious clay court event in the southern hemisphere. In 1970 she became the second woman to complete a Calendar Grand Slam. She was physically powerful — far more athletic than most women's players of her era — and dominated with her serve and her ability to cover the court. The main arena at the Australian Open is named in her honour.
fun_facts: She holds the record for most Grand Slam singles titles — 24 — more than anyone in history

players.name: Monica Seles
players.biography: Monica Seles was one of the most extraordinary natural talents in tennis history and her career was defined both by phenomenal achievement and terrible tragedy. The Yugoslav-born prodigy won nine Grand Slam singles titles before the age of 20 — including winning the French Open at 16. Her double-handed groundstrokes from both sides and her distinctive grunting became famous worldwide. In 1993, at the height of her powers, she was stabbed in the back by a deranged fan of Steffi Graf in Hamburg. She returned after two years away but was never quite the same. Despite this, her courage and resilience made her one of sport's most admired figures.

She won the French Open at just 16 years old
She was world number one at 17 — the youngest ever in women's tennis

players.name: Boris Becker
players.biography: Boris Becker became the youngest-ever Wimbledon champion at just 17 years old in 1985, capturing the world's attention with his red-haired exuberance, huge serve, and diving volleys. The Leimen-born German went on to win Wimbledon three times and six Grand Slam titles in total. His serve-and-volley style was perfectly suited to grass and his speed around the net was exceptional. His rivalry with Stefan Edberg — two contrasting play styles meeting in classic Wimbledon finals — was one of the great tennis rivalries. He went on to coach Novak Djokovic to six major titles between 2013 and 2016.

He was famous for diving full-length to volley at the net
He coached Novak Djokovic to 6 Grand Slams

players.name: Pete Sampras
players.biography: Pete Sampras was the greatest grass court player in tennis history and the dominant world number one through most of the 1990s. 'Pistol Pete' held the world number one ranking for 286 weeks and won 14 Grand Slam titles — a record that stood until Federer overtook him. His serve-and-volley style was devastating on fast surfaces, and his slice backhand set up countless net approaches. He won Wimbledon seven times — equalling the then-record — and closed his career with a US Open title in his final tournament in 2002. His grace, consistency, and unmatched tennis intelligence made him the gold standard of his era.

ATP year-end No.1 for 6 consecutive years

He won his final US Open in his very last professional match

players.name: Andre Agassi
players.biography: Andre Agassi is one of only eight men to complete the Career Grand Slam — winning all four major titles — and one of only five to also win Olympic gold. The flamboyant Las Vegas-born player went through extraordinary highs and lows: he admitted to drug use in his autobiography, his ranking fell to 141 before he fought back to world number one. His return of serve was the best in tennis history, and he won eight Grand Slams across a 20-year career. His open approach to mental health struggles and his outstanding school-building charity work in Las Vegas have made him one of sport's most admired figures.

He won Grand Slams on all four different surfaces — a very rare achievement

players.name: John McEnroe
players.biography: John McEnroe was the most gifted natural tennis player of his era — a left-hander with extraordinary touch, feel, and creativity who combined genius at the net with explosive arguing with umpires. His outbursts — particularly 'You cannot be serious!' at Wimbledon 1981 — are among sport's most iconic moments. Yet his tennis was sublime: his serve-and-volley game was flawless, his drop shots and lobs were strokes of genius, and his 1984 season — 82-3 — is statistically the best by any player. He won seven Grand Slams and was world number one for four years. Behind the anger was a tennis genius of the highest order.

His 1984 season record of 82-3 is statistically the greatest season in tennis history
He was as gifted with the guitar as with a tennis racquet

players.name: Jimmy Connors
players.biography: Jimmy Connors was the most combative and passionate tennis player ever — a fighter who dragged greatness from confrontation and crowd energy. He held the world number one ranking for a record 268 consecutive weeks and won eight Grand Slam titles. His two-handed backhand was one of tennis's first and most effective, and his baseline game combined relentless power with extraordinary foot speed. His 1991 US Open run — at age 39, coming from nowhere — when he reached the semi-finals and the New York crowd roared him on represents one of sport's great emotional moments. He played professional tennis for 25 years.

players.name: Ivan Lendl
players.biography: Ivan Lendl was the most disciplined, machine-like player in tennis history — a Czech perfectionist who pioneered the modern baseline game and modern sports science in tennis. He was world number one for 270 weeks and won eight Grand Slam titles, including the French Open three times. His relentless work ethic, physical conditioning, and groundstroke power made him the template for the modern baseline player. He was notable for his mental toughness in transforming from a player who lost in finals to a dominant champion. He later coached Andy Murray to his first Grand Slam title and two Wimbledon championships.

He coached Andy Murray to three Grand Slam titles

players.name: Stefan Edberg
players.biography: Stefan Edberg was the most elegant serve-and-volley player of the Open Era and a gentleman of tennis who won the ATP Sportsmanship Award eight times. The Swedish master won six Grand Slams, was world number one for 72 weeks, and his rivalry with Boris Becker — particularly in three Wimbledon finals between 1988 and 1990 — is one of tennis's finest series. His single-handed backhand volley was perhaps the most beautiful shot in tennis history. He won Wimbledon and the US Open twice each and was later the role model Roger Federer cited as his childhood hero and coach.

Roger Federer named him as his childhood hero and later hired him as his coach
His backhand volley is considered by many the most technically perfect shot in tennis history
players.style: Elegant serve-and-volley, perfect backhand volley, graceful athleticism, outstanding sportsmanship

players.name: Guillermo Vilas
players.biography: Guillermo Vilas was South America's first great tennis champion and Argentina's most beloved sportsman of his era. The Buenos Aires-born clay court king won four Grand Slam titles and his 1977 season — where he won 16 tournaments in a row — is one of the great individual seasons in tennis history. His heavy topspin groundstrokes and physical endurance on clay made him nearly unbeatable on the red dirt of Roland Garros and Buenos Aires. He was world number one in 1977 and is credited with inspiring Argentina's subsequent generation of great tennis players including Guillermo Coria and Juan Martín del Potro. He is also a published poet.

He is a published poet and intellectual known as 'The Poet of the Courts'
He inspired generations of Argentine tennis players after him

players.name: Michael Phelps
players.biography: Michael Phelps is the most decorated Olympian in history with 28 Olympic medals — 23 of them gold. At the 2008 Beijing Olympics he won 8 gold medals in 8 events, breaking Mark Spitz's record of 7. His physique seems designed by evolution for swimming: a 6'7" wingspan despite being 6'4" tall, size-14 feet that act as flippers, and a torso unusually long relative to his legs, which makes his swim stroke particularly efficient. He retired after 2012 London, returned for Rio 2016 and won five more gold medals. He has spoken powerfully about mental health struggles, helping to reduce stigma around the topic for athletes worldwide.

8 gold medals at one Olympics (2008 Beijing) — Olympic record

players.name: Usain Bolt
players.biography: Usain Bolt is the fastest human being ever recorded and the most celebrated sprinter in Olympic history. Born in Trelawny, Jamaica, he was a naturally gifted cricketer before switching to sprinting. At the 2008 Beijing Olympics, he broke the world record for the 100m while celebrating before the finish line, and broke the 200m world record as well. He went on to win 8 Olympic gold medals and 11 World Championship golds. His records — 9.58s for 100m and 19.19s for 200m — set at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin — have not been broken since. His charismatic personality and 'lightning bolt' celebration made him one of the most recognisable athletes in the world.

players.name: Carl Lewis
players.biography: Carl Lewis is the greatest track and field athlete in Olympic history. The New Jersey-born sprinter and long jumper won nine Olympic gold medals across four consecutive Games (1984-1996), tying Jesse Owens's four-gold record at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. His long jump gold at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics — his final Olympic appearance at age 35 — is considered one of the greatest sporting achievements of all time. He held the world 100m record and his long jump of 8.91m at the 1991 World Championships is still the second furthest ever jumped. He is widely considered the greatest athlete of the 20th century.
